mainTopic: The end of the חרש-and-sisters proofs about a קטן אוכל נבלות, the close of פרק חרש, and the new משנה on a wife's testimony that her husband died in war or other disasters
overview: The amud first finishes a צריכא: the ברייתא needed three cases (שרצים, דם, and טומאה for כהנים) to teach that adults may not actively cause children to sin, because each case has its own special feature. Then the גמרא tries to prove from the משנה of a חרש and a פקח married to two sisters that בית דין must stop a קטן אוכל נבלות. The first two cases are pushed off, because in each one the wife or the husband is a responsible person with an איסור of their own. רבא brings a case where both husband and wife are חרשים. רב שמעיה answers that the divorce there is only a גזירה, so people will not think the יבמה may marry an outsider. פרק חרש then ends. A new פרק opens with a משנה: a woman who says her husband died overseas is believed when there was peace at home and in the world, but not during war or after a fight, and רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about whether she must come crying. רבא explains that in war she may report what she only assumed. He then discusses famine, collapse, snakes, and plague, and the גמרא starts asking about a woman who is herself the only source for the war.

steps.title: Why the case of creeping creatures alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Continuing the צריכא: had the ברייתא taught only שרצים, we might think the rule is strict only because שרצים are forbidden in any amount, unlike דם.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it had taught only creeping creatures, I would say the rule is strict because they are forbidden in even a tiny amount. But blood, which is not forbidden until there is a רביעית, I would say is not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is in the middle of explaining why the ברייתא needed all three cases. Here it shows that the case of שרצים alone could not teach us about דם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שרץ is forbidden even when it is very small, so it is a stricter איסור. דם only becomes a full איסור at a set amount, so we might have thought it is lighter and an adult may feed it to a child. That is why דם had to be written separately.

keyTerms.meaning: In any amount, even a tiny bit
A quarter of a לוג, a liquid measure
I might say no, the rule does not apply

phrases.english: because their prohibition applies to any amount,
phrases.notes: "Their" means שרצים, the case the ברייתא listed just before.

phrases.english: but blood,
which is not forbidden until there is a quarter-log,
I would say not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא begun before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only שרצים are included, because they are forbidden in any amount
steps.terutzMaskana: דם must be listed too, since it has a minimum amount and might seem lighter

steps.title: Why the case of blood alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: Had the ברייתא taught only דם, we might think the rule is strict only because דם carries כרת, unlike שרצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught only blood, I would say it is strict because blood carries כרת. But creeping creatures I would say are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא flips it around and shows that the case of דם alone could not teach us about שרצים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Eating דם is punished with כרת, which makes it a very serious איסור. Eating שרצים has no כרת, so we might think it is lighter. So the ברייתא needed both cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a severe heavenly punishment

phrases.english: And if it had taught us blood,
that is because there is karet,
but creeping creatures, I would say not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 1: blood cannot teach שרצים
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only דם is included, because it carries כרת
steps.terutzMaskana: שרצים must be listed too, since they have no כרת

steps.title: Why food prohibitions alone would not teach about impurity
steps.stepSummary: Had the ברייתא taught only שרצים and דם, we might think the rule applies only to איסורים that apply to every Jew, not to טומאה for כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us these two, I would say it is because their prohibition is the same for everyone. But impurity, I would say not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now groups שרצים and דם together and shows they still could not teach us the third case, טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שרצים and דם are forbidden to every Jew. The איסור of becoming טמא to the dead applies only to כהנים, so we might think it is weaker and an adult may make a young כהן טמא. That is why טומאה had to be listed too.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritual impurity; here, a כהן becoming טמא

phrases.english: And if it had taught us these two,
that is because their prohibition is equal for all,
but impurity, I would say not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines steps 1 and 2 and contrasts them with טומאה
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only איסורים that apply to everyone are included
steps.terutzMaskana: טומאה of כהנים must be listed too

steps.title: Why impurity alone would not be enough, so all three cases are needed
steps.stepSummary: Had the ברייתא taught only טומאה, we might think כהנים are special because they have extra מצוות. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it had taught us impurity, I would say כהנים are different, because the Torah gave them extra מצוות. But these others, I would say not. So all of them are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows the last piece: טומאה alone could not teach about food איסורים. Then it closes with צריכא, meaning all three cases were needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים were given extra מצוות, so the Torah may be stricter with them, even with young ones. From that alone we could not learn that adults may not feed a child שרצים or דם. Since every case has its own feature, none can be learned from another, and all three must be written.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; all the cases are necessary

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא lists שרצים, דם, and טומאה because each has a special feature (any amount, כרת, applies to all, extra מצוות for כהנים). No case could be learned from the others, so all three are needed.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us impurity,
priests are different,
because He gave them extra מצוות,
but these, I would say not,
therefore it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 3, then closes the whole צריכא
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each case has a unique feature
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only טומאה of כהנים is included, because כהנים have extra מצוות

steps.title: New source: a deaf-mute and a competent brother married to two sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: two brothers, a חרש and a פקח, are married to two sisters. If the חרש dies, his widow leaves without יבום or חליצה, because she is the פקח's wife's sister.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two brothers, one competent and one a deaf-mute, are married to two competent sisters. If the deaf-mute husband dies, what does the competent brother do? She goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
steps.whatsHappening: With תא שמע, the גמרא starts bringing a new source on its larger topic. For now it is only quoting the case. The point it wants to prove comes later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש's marriage is valid only מדרבנן, so his widow's tie to the brother is weak. She is also the פקח's wife's sister, who is forbidden to him. So she is released with no יבום and no חליצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; brings a source to help answer a question
A competent person who can hear and speak
A deaf-mute, treated as not fully responsible in הלכה
Wife's sister, forbidden to marry while the wife is alive

steps.confusionAlert: This is not yet a proof. The גמרא is only quoting the משנה here. What it learns from the case comes in the next lines.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: two brothers, one competent and one deaf-mute,
married to two competent sisters.
If the deaf-mute, husband of a competent woman, died,
what should the competent one, husband of a competent woman, do?
She goes out because she is his wife's sister.
phrases.notes: "Goes out" means she is free to remarry, with no יבום and no חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ וְאֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the צריכא to a new source for the larger question
steps.raayaObject: The larger question being discussed: what we must do about someone not responsible for מצוות doing an איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about a חרש and a פקח married to two sisters

steps.title: The reverse case: the competent brother dies
steps.stepSummary: If the פקח dies, the חרש must divorce his own wife with a גט, and his brother's widow is forbidden to him forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the competent husband dies, what does the deaf-mute husband do? He sends away his wife with a גט, and his brother's wife is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה, now with the opposite case. It is still setting up the source for the inference that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the dead brother's marriage was fully valid, so the widow's tie to the חרש comes from the Torah. That tie is stronger than the חרש's own marriage, which is only מדרבנן, so he must divorce his wife. Yet the widow stays forbidden to him forever.

phrases.english: If the competent one, husband of a competent woman, died,
what should the deaf-mute, husband of a competent woman, do?
He divorces his wife with a bill of divorce,
and his brother's wife is forbidden forever.
phrases.notes: As a חרש he can't do חליצה with her, and יבום isn't possible either, so she stays tied to him with no way out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same משנה, the reverse case of step 5
steps.raayaObject: The same larger question; the inference is drawn after this quote
steps.raayaSupportSource: Second case of the משנה: the חרש divorces his wife and the widow is forbidden forever

steps.title: Why force the deaf-mute to divorce his wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its proof from the משנה. If a חרש is like a קטן אוכל נבלות, whom we need not stop, why must he divorce his wife?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why does he have to divorce his wife with a גט? Let her stay with him. He is like a child eating forbidden meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out why the משנה from steps 5–6 looks like a proof. Someone forced the חרש to divorce, so it seems בית דין must stop a non-responsible person from doing wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חרש is not legally responsible, like a קטן eating נבלות. If בית דין had no duty to stop such a person, the משנה would just leave him with his wife. Since the משנה forces a גט, it seems בית דין must step in.

keyTerms.meaning: A child eating non-kosher meat: the classic case of a person who is not responsible doing something forbidden

phrases.english: Why does he divorce his wife with a bill of divorce?
phrases.notes: This is the חרש from step 6. His wife became forbidden to him once her sister fell to him for יבום.

phrases.english: Let her stay with him,
he is like a minor eating forbidden meat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי מוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּגֵט? תִּיתִּיב גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in steps 5–6
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop a non-responsible person from doing an איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's ruling that the חרש must divorce his wife

steps.title: The wife is responsible, so the prohibition is hers
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. The divorce is required because of the wife's own איסור, since she is a פקחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the prohibition that is on her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof. The divorce is not about stopping the חרש. It is because his wife is fully responsible and must not live with a man forbidden to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In that משנה the two sisters were both פקחות. So even if we never have to stop the חרש, his wife is fully responsible and is herself doing an איסור. The proof says nothing about a case where nobody involved is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: Her prohibition: the איסור that the responsible wife herself carries
A woman who is legally competent (hears and speaks)

phrases.english: Because of the prohibition on her.
phrases.notes: In that משנה both sisters are fully competent, so the wife herself is responsible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof made in step 7
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the first משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A responsible person (the wife) is involved, so the divorce can be because of her own איסור

steps.title: A second case: two competent brothers, one deaf-mute sister
steps.stepSummary: Another case from the same משנה: two פקחים are married to two sisters, one פקחת and one חרשת. If the husband of the פקחת dies, the husband of the חרשת must divorce his wife and do חליצה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: Two competent brothers are married to two sisters, one competent and one a deaf-mute. If the competent husband of the deaf-mute dies, what does the competent husband of the competent sister do? The widow leaves, since she is his wife's sister. If the competent husband of the competent sister dies, what does the competent husband of the deaf-mute do? He divorces his wife with a גט, and does חליצה with his brother's widow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case that again ends with a man forced to divorce his wife. It is setting up another try at the same proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the wife being divorced is the חרשת, the one who is not responsible. If we have no duty to stop a non-responsible person, why should she have to leave?

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear: the גמרא brings a source as proof
A deaf-mute woman, not legally responsible
A wife's sister, forbidden while the wife is alive
The ceremony that frees a widow from יבום

phrases.english: Come and hear: two competent brothers
married to two sisters,
one competent and one a deaf-mute.
If the competent husband of the deaf-mute died,
what should the competent husband of the competent sister do?
She goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
If the competent husband of the competent sister died,
what should the competent husband of the deaf-mute do?
He divorces his wife with a bill of divorce,
and frees his brother's wife with חליצה.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי אַחִין פִּקְחִין נְשׂוּאִין שְׁתֵּי אֲחָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed off, a new source is brought
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop a non-responsible person from doing an איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ruling that the husband of the חרשת must divorce her

steps.title: Why must the deaf-mute wife leave?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא again asks: the חרשת is like a קטן אוכל נבלות, so why not let her stay?
steps.simpleTranslation: But why does he divorce his wife with a גט? Let her stay with him. She is like a child eating forbidden meat!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the same inference from the new case. Forcing a divorce suggests that בית דין must stop a non-responsible person, here the חרשת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are almost the same as step 7, but the target is different. Now the one who is like a קטן is the wife, the חרשת. If no one had to stop her, the divorce would seem unnecessary.

phrases.english: But why does he divorce his wife with a bill of divorce?
Let her stay with him,
she is like a minor eating forbidden meat!
phrases.notes: Here it is the deaf-mute wife who is not responsible.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי מוֹצִיא אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ בְּגֵט? תִּיתֵּיב גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the case in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop a non-responsible person from doing an איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: The forced divorce of the חרשת

steps.title: The husband is responsible, so the prohibition is his
steps.stepSummary: Pushed off again. The divorce is required because the husband is a פקח, and the איסור is his own.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of the prohibition that is on him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects this proof the same way. The husband is fully responsible, so he himself may not stay with a woman forbidden to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 pointed to the wife. Here the responsible person is the husband. Either way, a responsible person is involved, so the case cannot show what happens when no one is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: His prohibition: the איסור that the responsible husband himself carries

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up דִידַהּ (hers, step 8) with דִּידֵיהּ (his, here). The answer changes because now the responsible one is the husband.

phrases.english: Because of the prohibition on him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 10, in the same way as step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the second case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The husband is a פקח, so the divorce can be because of his own איסור

steps.title: רבא's case: both husband and wife are deaf-mutes
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a case where a חרש is married to a חרשת. Even so, when the פקח brother dies, the חרש must divorce his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come hear: Two brothers, one a deaf-mute and one competent, are married to two sisters, one competent and one a deaf-mute. If the deaf-mute husband of the deaf-mute dies, what does the competent husband of the competent sister do? The widow leaves, since she is his wife's sister. If the competent husband of the competent sister dies, what does the deaf-mute husband of the deaf-mute do? He divorces his wife with a גט, and his brother's widow is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a case where neither the husband nor the wife is responsible, and still a divorce is required. This sets up a proof that the earlier pushbacks cannot answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 8 and 11 escaped by pointing to a responsible wife, then a responsible husband. Here both are חרשים, so there is no "her איסור" or "his איסור" to point to. The forced divorce seems to show that בית דין must step in even when no one involved is responsible.

keyTerms.meaning: A deaf-mute man, not legally responsible

steps.whyThisMatters: This case blocks both earlier answers, which makes it the strongest evidence so far that בית דין must stop non-responsible people from doing an איסור.

phrases.english: Rava said: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ
phrases.english: two brothers, one a deaf-mute and one competent,
married to two sisters,
one competent and one a deaf-mute.
If the deaf-mute husband of the deaf-mute died,
what should the competent husband of the competent sister do?
She goes free, because she is his wife's sister.
If the competent husband of the competent sister died,
what should the deaf-mute husband of the deaf-mute do?
He divorces his wife with a bill of divorce,
and his brother's wife is forbidden to him forever.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא, תָּא שְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי אַחִין, אֶחָד חֵרֵשׁ וְאֶחָד פִּקֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds a case that gets around both earlier pushbacks
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop a non-responsible person from doing an איסור
steps.raayaSupportSource: A case where a חרש married to a חרשת is still forced to divorce

steps.title: No one has an איסור here, yet he must still divorce
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his proof. In the case of a חרש married to a חרשת, neither the wife nor the husband has their own איסור, yet the משנה still says he must divorce her.
steps.simpleTranslation: But here there is no איסור on her and no איסור on him, and yet the משנה teaches that he sends his wife away with a גט!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא spells out why his case is stronger than the earlier ones. Both earlier pushbacks are blocked here, so the divorce seems to prove that we stop even a קטן אוכל נבלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the divorce was because of the wife's own איסור (she was a פקחת). Step 11 said it was because of the husband's own איסור (he was a פקח). Here both are deaf, so neither excuse works, and the משנה still demands a divorce.

keyTerms.meaning: He sends her away with a bill of divorce

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָאו אִיסּוּרָא דִידַהּ אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: But here, where there is no prohibition of hers,
phrases.notes: She is a חרשת, so the earlier answer from Step 8, that it was her own איסור, doesn't fit.

phrases.english: and there is no prohibition of his,
phrases.notes: He is a חרש too, so the answer from Step 11 doesn't fit either.

phrases.english: and yet it teaches: he sends away his wife with a divorce document!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא דְּלָאו אִיסּוּרָא דִידַהּ אִיכָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 12 by showing that both earlier pushbacks fail here.
steps.raayaObject: That בית דין must stop even a קטן אוכל נבלות, meaning someone who is not responsible for the איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of a חרש married to a חרשת who must divorce her when his פקח brother dies.

steps.title: The divorce is only a rabbinic safeguard
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה answers that the divorce is a גזירה. It keeps people from wrongly thinking the widowed יבמה may marry anyone she likes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said: It is a rabbinic decree, made so people will not permit a יבמה to marry an outsider.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה pushes off רבא's proof. The divorce here has nothing to do with stopping a child from an איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People might think the חרשת is a fully married wife. That would make the widow the חרש's אחות אשה, free to marry anyone without יבום or חליצה. In truth the deaf couple's marriage is not a full Torah marriage, so the widow is still tied to the יבם. The חכמים required a divorce so no one would make this mistake. That means the case proves nothing about a קטן אוכל נבלות.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
Wrongly permitting a widow waiting for יבום to marry an outsider
Literally 'the market'; here it means anyone outside the family

steps.whatToRemember: All the proofs in this סוגיא get pushed off. These cases give no clear proof on whether בית דין must stop a קטן אוכל נבלות.

phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said:
It is a decree because of permitting a yevama to the marketplace.
phrases.notes: People might think the widow is the wife's sister and so free to marry any man, which she really isn't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 13 by giving a different reason for the divorce.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full: the case no longer proves anything about a קטן אוכל נבלות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the divorce was about stopping an איסור. It is really a גזירה to prevent a public mistake about the יבמה.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק חרש
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of פרק חרש.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק חרש.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the chapter of חרש. It is a traditional farewell said when finishing a פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new argument is made here. It marks the boundary before a new משנה and a new topic begin.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you, the closing formula of a פרק
A deaf-mute; also the name of the פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Deaf-mute'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek after the final pushback.

steps.title: A woman is believed when there was peace at home and in the world
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. A woman went overseas with her husband and returned alone saying he died. If there was peace between them and peace in the world, she may remarry, or do יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman went overseas with her husband. There was peace between them and peace in the world. She came back and said 'My husband died.' She may marry someone else. If she says 'My husband died,' she may also do יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The new פרק opens with its basic rule: a woman's own word about her husband's death is accepted when nothing makes it suspicious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally one witness is not enough, but here the woman herself is believed. The two kinds of peace matter because the next part of the משנה describes the opposite situations.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace in the world, meaning no war
She may marry her husband's brother through יבום

phrases.aramaic: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם.
phrases.english: A woman who went, she and her husband, overseas.
There is peace between him and her, and peace in the world.
And she came and said 'My husband died' — she may marry.
'My husband died' — she may enter levirate marriage.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהָלְכָה הִיא וּבַעְלָהּ לִמְדִינַת הַיָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman who says her husband died overseas is believed, and may remarry or do יבום, when there was peace between them and peace in the world.

steps.title: With war or a family fight, she is not believed
steps.stepSummary: If there was war in the world, or a fight between husband and wife, her claim that he died is not accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there was peace between them but war in the world, or a fight between them but peace in the world, and she came and said 'My husband died,' she is not believed.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now gives the opposite cases, where her word is not accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a war she may honestly be mistaken, for example by assuming he died when she did not see it. After a fight she may be lying because she wants to be rid of him. Either one is enough to take away her believability.

phrases.english: Peace between him and her, and war in the world.
A quarrel between him and her, and peace in the world.
And she came and said 'My husband died' — she is not believed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the contrasting cases to Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: War in the world or a quarrel between them makes her not believed.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: only if she comes crying with torn clothes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says she is never believed unless she arrives crying with her clothes torn.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: She is never believed, unless she came crying and her clothes were torn.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a stricter opinion. He demands visible signs of mourning before trusting her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, even peace at home and in the world is not enough. Only signs of real grief show that her report is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Her clothes are torn, a sign of mourning

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: She is never believed,
unless she came crying,
and her clothes are torn.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לְעוֹלָם אֵינָהּ נֶאֱמֶנֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a stricter, opposing view to the ruling of the first opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: She is believed only if she returns crying with torn clothes.

steps.title: The חכמים: crying or not, she may marry
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reject רבי יהודה's requirement. Whether she comes crying or not, she may marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Both this one and that one may marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer רבי יהודה and turn down his extra requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, crying and torn clothes add nothing. As long as the situation is not suspicious (no war and no fight), her word is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule of this new פרק: a woman is believed about her husband's death unless war or a fight makes her report doubtful. רבי יהודה's demand for signs of mourning is not accepted by the חכמים.

phrases.english: They said to him:
Both this one and that one may marry.
phrases.notes: Both the woman who comes crying and the one who doesn't.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַחַת זוֹ וְאַחַת זוֹ תִּנָּשֵׂא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי יהודה's view from Step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Full rejection of רבי יהודה's requirement.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Crying and torn clothes are not needed for her to be believed.

steps.title: Why the משנה mentions 'peace'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה said 'peace between them' and 'peace in the world' only to set up the contrast with 'a fight between them' and 'war in the world.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה taught 'peace between him and her' because it wanted to go on and teach 'a fight between him and her.' It taught 'peace in the world' because it wanted to go on and teach 'war in the world.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by explaining the wording of the משנה. It says the word 'peace' was written mainly to set up the cases of fighting and war that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think peace is a special condition she must prove before she is believed. The גמרא says no: the משנה wrote 'peace' only as the opposite of the cases that really matter. What actually takes away her credibility is a fight with her husband or a war.

keyTerms.meaning: Because it wanted to go on and teach

phrases.english: גמרא: It taught 'peace between him and her'
because it wanted to teach 'a fight between him and her.'
It taught 'peace in the world'
because it wanted to teach 'war in the world.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא שָׁלוֹם בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ מִשּׁוּם דְּקָבָעֵי לְמִיתְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה by explaining its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Peace' in the משנה is written only as a contrast to fighting and war, which are the real factors that take away her credibility.

steps.title: רבא: in war she reports what she assumes
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains why she is not believed during war: she may say what she imagines happened, assuming that he could not have survived when so many others were killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: What is the reason for the rule about war? Because she says what she imagines happened. She thinks: can it be that, with all these people killed, he alone escaped?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the reason the משנה does not believe her in wartime. Her claim may come from guessing, not from seeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She is not suspected of lying on purpose. The worry is an honest mistake. Because so many people died around her, she assumes her husband died too, even if she never saw it.

keyTerms.meaning: Based on what she imagines or assumes

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying she lies. He is saying she honestly believes something she did not actually see.

phrases.english: Rava said:
What is the reason for the rule about war?
Because she says what she imagines.
Could it enter one's mind that among all these who were killed,
phrases.notes: This is what the woman says to herself.

phrases.english: he escaped?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה's war rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: During war she is not believed because she may testify based on an assumption.

steps.title: But she loves him, so she would check carefully
steps.stepSummary: רבא raises a possible objection: since there was peace between them, she would surely wait until she actually saw him die.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: since there was peace between him and her, she waits until she actually sees it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא raises a possible challenge to his own reason, and the next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The objection says a loving wife would not jump to conclusions. Because she cares about him, she would wait until she was sure he was dead. If so, the fear of guessing should not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say; an expected objection

phrases.english: If you will say,
since there is peace between him and her,
she waits until she sees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's reason that she says what she imagines.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that she says what she imagines (step 21).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wife on good terms with her husband would be careful and wait to see his death, so she would not be guessing.

steps.title: Even what she sees can mislead her
steps.stepSummary: Even if she sees him struck by an arrow or spear, she may think he is surely dead, yet someone may treat him with medicine and he survives.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sometimes they strike him with an arrow or a spear, and she thinks he is certainly dead. But someone may prepare medicine for him, and he lives.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the objection. Even a careful wife who sees something with her own eyes can still be wrong in wartime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her waiting does not solve the problem. In war she might see a wound that looks deadly and leave, sure that he has died. People sometimes recover from such wounds, so even what she saw is not proof of death.
steps.whatToRemember: In war, even an honest and caring wife may report a death she did not truly confirm, so she is not believed.

phrases.aramaic: זִימְנִין דְּמָחוּ לֵיהּ בְּגִירָא אוֹ בְּרוּמְחָא
phrases.english: Sometimes they strike him with an arrow or a spear
and she thinks he is certainly dead,
but there is someone who prepares medicine, and he lives.

steps.triggerLanguage: זִימְנִין דְּמָחוּ לֵיהּ בְּגִירָא אוֹ בְּרוּמְחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that even seeing does not give certainty in wartime
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A loving wife waits until she sees, so she is reliable.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even what she sees, a deadly-looking wound, can mislead her, so she is still not believed.

steps.title: רבא's first view: famine is not like war
steps.stepSummary: רבא first thought that in a famine she is believed, since she would not report a death based on assumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא thought to say that famine is not like war, because in a famine she does not say what she imagines.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new case, famine, and gives רבא's first opinion about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's first thought was that in famine there is no chaos like a battlefield. A wife would be with her husband and see what really happened, so the fear of guessing would not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא thought to say; a view he later takes back

steps.confusionAlert: 'סבר למימר' signals a view רבא will take back. Do not treat it as his final ruling.

phrases.english: Rava thought to say
famine is not like war,
since she does not say what she imagines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבא's reasoning about war to a new case, famine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First view: in famine she is believed, since there is no fear she is guessing.

steps.title: רבא changes his mind: famine is like war
steps.stepSummary: רבא takes back his first view and rules that famine is like war.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: Famine is like war.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא reverses his first opinion. The next step tells the story that made him change his mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now רבא holds that in famine too she may report a death based on an assumption. So she is not believed in famine, just as in war.

keyTerms.meaning: He then said; he changed his mind

phrases.english: Rava then said:
Famine is like war.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא takes back the view in step 24.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's own first view that famine is not like war.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In famine too a woman may report a death she only assumed.

steps.title: The woman whose husband died in a famine
steps.stepSummary: A woman told רבא her husband died of hunger. When he questioned her, her answer showed she had left him alive and only assumed he died.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman came before רבא and said: 'My husband died in the famine.' He said to her: 'You did well to save yourself! Do you think that with that little bit of flour you left him, he could have lived?' She said: 'The master also knows that in such a situation a person cannot live.'
steps.whatsHappening: This story explains why רבא changed his mind. By questioning her, he found that she had not seen her husband die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא cleverly spoke as if he agreed with her, and she admitted she had run away and left him with a little food. She stated he was dead only because she assumed he could not survive. This shows that in famine, too, a woman can say what she imagines.

phrases.english: For a certain woman came before Rava,
she said to him: 'My husband died in the famine.'
He said to her: You did well
that you saved yourself?
phrases.notes: רבא is testing her, speaking as though he agrees she was right to run away.

phrases.english: Do you think
that with that little bit of sifted flour
that you left him, he would have lived?
She said to him: The master also knows
that in a case like this, one does not live.
phrases.notes: Her answer shows she left him alive and only assumed he died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the case that caused רבא's change of mind in step 25.
steps.raayaObject: That famine is like war, since a woman can report a death she only assumed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: An actual case of a woman who testified before רבא.

steps.title: רבא's final view: famine is stricter than war
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that famine is even worse than war. In war she is believed if she says he died in bed. In famine she is believed only if she says 'he died and I buried him.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא then said: Famine is worse than war. In war, only when she says 'my husband died in the war' is she not believed. But if she says 'he died in his bed,' she is believed. In famine, however, she is not believed until she says, 'He died and I buried him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא changes his mind again and gives his final position. Famine is not just like war; it needs an even stronger claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In war, the doubt comes only from the battle itself, so a claim of a different kind of death is believed. In famine, hunger affects everyone everywhere, so any claim of death could be a guess. Therefore she must say she actually buried him.

keyTerms.meaning: He died and I buried him

steps.whatToRemember: Final view of רבא: in war, a woman is not believed only if she says he died in the war. In famine, she is believed only if she says, 'He died and I buried him.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for what a woman must say during famine before she may remarry.

phrases.english: Rava then said:
Famine is worse than war.
For with war,
when she says, 'My husband died in the war,'
that is when she is not believed,
but if she says 'he died in his bed,' she is believed.
Whereas with famine,
not until she says, 'He died and I buried him.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר רָבָא רְעָבוֹן גְּרִיעָה מִמִּלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא goes a step further than step 25: famine is not only like war but stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In famine she is believed only if she says she buried him. In war, only a claim that he died in the war is not believed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Famine requires 'he died and I buried him'; in war a claim of a death unrelated to the war is believed.

steps.title: Collapses and snake attacks are like war
steps.stepSummary: A מפולת (collapse) and a release of snakes and scorpions are treated like war, because the wife may report his death based on assumption.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a building collapsed, it is like war, because she may say he died based on what she imagines. If snakes and scorpions were let loose, that is also like war, for the same reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds two more disasters to the list of situations that count like war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In war, the worry is that a wife assumes her husband died without truly seeing it. The same worry applies to a collapse or a deadly animal attack. In such chaos she may think nobody could have survived, so her report may be a guess and not something she saw.

keyTerms.meaning: A collapse, such as a building falling down
Based on assumption, what one imagines happened
A release or attack of snakes and scorpions
Like war, with the same stricter rule for her testimony

phrases.english: A collapse — it is like war,
since she speaks based on assumption.
A sending of snakes and scorpions —
they are like war,
since she speaks based on assumption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends רבא's comparison of famine to war to other disasters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Collapses and snake or scorpion attacks follow the rules of war, because the wife may report a death based on assumption.

steps.title: Dispute whether plague is like war
steps.stepSummary: For דבר (plague), one view says it is like war because of assumption. The other view says it is not, because people know that even in plague no one dies before his time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Plague: some say it is like war and some say it is not. Those who say it is like war hold that people speak based on assumption. Those who say it is not like war rely on the popular saying: 'Plague lasted seven years, and no one died before his time.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opinions about plague and explains the reason for each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view: in plague so many die that a wife may assume her husband died too. The second view: everyone knows people often survive a plague, so she would not assume he died. If she says he died, she must have actually seen it.

keyTerms.meaning: Without his years, before his set time

steps.confusionAlert: The saying does not mean nobody dies in a plague. It means people survive or die according to their set time, so a plague does not make death certain.

phrases.aramaic: דֶּבֶר — אָמְרִי לַהּ הֲרֵי הוּא כְּמִלְחָמָה,
phrases.english: Plague — some say it is like war,
and some say it is not like war.
Some say it is like war,
since people speak based on assumption.
And some say it is not like war,
because they rely on what people say:
"Seven years there was plague,
and no person went before his time."

steps.triggerLanguage: דֶּבֶר — אָמְרִי לַהּ הֲרֵי הוּא כְּמִלְחָמָה, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אֵינוֹ כְּמִלְחָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of disasters, but this one has a dispute.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a dispute whether plague follows the rules of war. It depends on whether a wife would assume her husband's death during a plague.
steps.whatToRemember: Every case in this list turns on one question: in this disaster, would a wife report her husband's death based only on assumption?

steps.title: Is she believed when she herself says there was a war
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about a wife who is the only source for the claim that there was a war. Maybe we should believe her, since she had no reason to bring up the war if she were lying.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: if she herself is the one who said there was a war, what is the law? Do we say, why would she lie?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and starts the first side of it. The other side continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a wife is not fully believed about her husband's death in wartime. Here, though, the court only knows about the war because she told them. Had she wanted to lie, she could have simply left the war out. So perhaps the rule of מה לה לשקר makes her believed.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, introducing an open question
She established or claimed, here meaning she is the one who said there was a war
Do we say, introducing the first side of a question
Why would she lie? A reason to believe someone who could have made a better false claim

steps.whyThisMatters: This question tests whether מה לה לשקר can overcome the worry about assumption in wartime.

phrases.english: It was asked of them:
If she herself established a war in the world,
phrases.notes: The court didn't know about any war. She is the one who told them, and she says he died in it.

phrases.english: what is the law?
Do we say: why would she lie,
phrases.notes: If she were lying, she could have just said he died without mentioning any war.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֶחְזִיקָה הִיא מִלְחָמָה בָּעוֹלָם, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from listing disasters like war to a new case where the war itself is known only from her words.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a wife is believed that her husband died in a war that only she reports, because of מה לה לשקר.
